In the present case, victim had remained consistent in her statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. as well as under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that the applicant took advantage of friendship with her, administered her a sedative drink and thereafter not only raped her, but took her unsolicited photographs also and under the threat of posting the same on social platforms, applicant repeatedly raped the victim and also considering that the applicant has a criminal history where he is an accused for serious charge of murder and attempt to murder and in case the applicant is released on bail, there is likelihood that he will try to influence the victim,

, at this stage, I do not find any merit in the argument of learned counsel for Harisudan Verma vs State Of U.P. on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4770386/

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for applicant submits that in first bail order certain aspect has not been noted that there was a material contradiction between statement of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.

He further submits that under supervisory power certain investigation was conducted wherein certain allegation was not found proved and that after rejection of first bail application incomplete examination-in-chief of PW-1 was recorded and thereafter she was not appearing and even bailable warrants were issued.

4. In order to consider argument of learned counsel for applicant, I have carefully perused statement of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and only difference is that specific word ?Balatkar? is not used in statement of victim under Section 161 Cr.P.C., however, other allegations which led to incident, are consistent.
Further, the statement recorded before Magistrate has more value so far as investigation is concerned.
Since cognizance has been taken of offence and charges are framed after perusal of entire charge sheet, therefore, at present there are more than prima facie case against applicant.
5. The only argument which can be considered at this stage is that prosecution witnesses are not coming forward to record their testimony.

First bail application was rejected on 31.05.2022, i.e.,
only ten months ago, therefore, the case will not fall under prolong detention.
The prayer for bail is accordingly rejected.

6. However, considering that witnesses are not coming forward to record their statement, the application is disposed of with direction to Trial Court to take all coercive measures to record statement of prosecution witnesses within eight weeks from today, if there is no other legal impediment.
Superintendent of Police concerned is also directed to ensure presence of witnesses as and when required by Trial Court.
Thereafter applicant is at liberty to file fresh application for bail before Trial Court.
